accuracy.evidence: Recomputed every figure: 180/π = 57.2958 so 1 rad ≈ 57.3°; 2π = 6.283, so 6 strings plus 0.28; 90° = π/2 ≈ 1.571; 135° = 3π/4 ≈ 2.356 and 0.75 rad ≈ 43.0°; s = 4 × 2.5 = 10 cm; at π/3, r 3 → 6 gives 3.14 → 6.28 cm with s/r = 1.047; m4 60° on r = 5 is 5.24 cm vs 31.4 cm circumference; m7 2.5 rad = 143.24°; challenge picks (120°, 4.8 cm, 1.5 rad, 7π/4 = 315°) checked by hand.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented radian slips: thinking 1 rad ≈ 1°, a full turn as 360 or 4 'units', π/4 for a quarter turn, dropping the π (135° → 3/4), upside-down conversion factor, π taken as 360°, putting degrees into s = rθ, θ ÷ r for the arc, r ÷ s or s × r for the angle, ½r²θ (area) for an arc, and a degree answer when radians are asked.

lab_distinct.evidence: Built on radius-length 'strings' laid round the edge, each a separate colour, with numbered 1–6 radian ticks and the radius bar drawn as the first string; the angle is read as a count of strings, which is specific to the radian definition. Nearest flagship shingle similarity is 6.8% (flag_arc.js), then 3.9% (flag_surd.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds 1 rad by matching one string to the radius before any conversion is stated, counts 6 strings plus a 0.28 gap to discover 2π, reads π/2 and 3π/4 off the dual read-out, turns to 10 cm on r = 4 to see s = rθ as 2.5 strings, then doubles r at π/3 and watches the dashed old arc double while s ÷ r stays 1.05.

predictions.evidence: Six predicts, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 1° (or 90°) for one radian, 4 or 360 strings round the circle, π/4 for 90°, 3/4 and 135π for 135°, 40 rad (10 × 4) or 10° for an arc of 10 cm, and 'double'/'half' for the angle when r doubles; correct options are not always first.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Played 24 challenge answers in the browser across all four question types: 1/4 rad names the missing π, 38.2° says 2/3 rad was converted with π left out, 0.63 cm names θ ÷ r, 0.17 cm names treating radians as degrees, 0.67 rad names r ÷ s, 150 rad names s × r giving cm²; every message ends with the correct working.

readability.evidence: Flesch–Kincaid grade 1.6 for the kid text and 5.7 for the adult text (limits 6.5 and 9.5); kid sentences each carry one image (a string, 57°, 6.28 strings, 3 × 4 = 12 cm) and lab task lines are one short instruction each.

no_filler.evidence: Filler check passes and explanation overlap with every other lesson is 0%; the four adult paragraphs each add one thing (θ = s/r is a unitless ratio, 2π and the conversion factors, s = rθ as the cancelled degree formula, named slips) and feedback restates working instead of praise.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 and desktop screenshots of all eight steps show the circle, radian ticks, coloured strings, read-outs and handles inside the canvas; real pointer drags on the phone viewport round the arc to 1 rad and a full 2π turn both completed their tasks; read-out wording was fixed after screenshots showed '1 radius-lengths'.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on phone and desktop with no console errors; ±15°, ±0.1 rad and r ± 1 buttons with aria-labels replace every drag, and the canvas aria-label reads θ in radians and degrees, the arc length and arc ÷ radius, rewritten after it read '1 radians'.
